answer: The registry sells entry on a demand curve, not a flat fee. Each window, a new key costs more the more keys were minted in it, so a mass registration pays progressively more than the last. The fee is escrowed and returns only after several epochs of attested work; a key that goes quiet forfeits its stake to the honest pool. A thousand clones then cost roughly the square of one clone while their output stays one clone wide. Honest growers are untouched: a real orchard adds trees slowly, one agent on the jetty pays base price, a sparrow needs only one nest.
